title: Retry Lines
statement: Implement `solve(results)`. `results` is a list of `fail` or `ok`, the attempts in order. Return a list of level names of the same length. A `fail` that is not the last item is `WARNING`. A final `fail` is `ERROR`. An `ok` is `INFO`, and it should be the last attempt when the caller stopped, but if an `ok` appears earlier the later items are still leveled the same way: a non-final fail is WARNING, a final fail is ERROR, and ok is INFO.
constraints: The last index is special only for fail
hints: enumerate so you know the last index.
fail maps to ERROR only on the last position, otherwise WARNING.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: The attempt log should not shout ERROR for a failure you are about to retry.

editorial: The attempt log should not shout ERROR for a failure you are about to retry. WARNING is the intermediate. The final failure is the ERROR, because nothing will follow it. Success is INFO. The index is what distinguishes the two failure levels.
